prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1327; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a rear-end collision at a signalled intersection and the claimant said the other vehicle struck the rear bumper while stopped. The claimant reported a knee injury and no lawyer is involved.

Entry 2: Obtained photos of both vehicles and the police report, which lists the claimant as a passenger in the vehicle at the time. The rear damage on the claimant's car lines up with the impact described.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who independently confirmed the stop and the rear impact. Two witnesses at the scene also gave statements that match the sequence of events.

Entry 4: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the vehicle history or the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 5: Reviewed the claimant's medical records, which describe a knee injury consistent with this type of collision. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so I've requested the treating provider's notes on the recovery plan.

Entry 6: The claimant has no record of prior injury to the same knee and reported none during the interview. Prior vehicle damage was also checked and none is on file for this car.

Entry 7: Each conversation with the claimant has produced the same account of the collision, including the stop, the impact, and the sequence afterward. No discrepancies have come up, and the file is ready for the coverage and damages review.
